ui.page.title: Heist Planner
ui.meta.description: Plan GTA Online heists: pick setups like the in-game board, work out payouts by difficulty and team size, see every deduction, set cuts and view entry and escape points on the map.
ui.nav.label: Pages
ui.side.patch: Figures based on Title Update 1.73 (Jul 2026) • Plan the finale • Work out the cuts • Get recommendations
ui.foot.data: Loot values are collected from community in-game testing after Title Update 1.73 (14 Jul 2026), e.g. GTA BOOM, Timesaver and GTA Boss. Rockstar confirmed the first-run-of-the-week bonus but never published the multipliers, so values marked ≈ are estimates, and secondary loot is random every run. Use this page for planning; these are not official figures.

ui.coach.name: Recommendations
ui.kortz.tag: Rob the hilltop art museum in Pacific Bluffs at night: go down to the basement vault, swap the real painting for a forgery from your mansion's Art Studio, then deliver the art to Alec in Cypress Flats.
ui.kortz.first: Selling the week's first main painting
ui.kortz.firstHint: The first painting sold after the Thursday reset pays 4×; after that the art market is saturated.
ui.kortz.paintingHint: The main painting rotates weekly; prices follow the difficulty and conditions you picked.
ui.kortz.bagsHint: A gallery painting takes about half a bag • values are estimates
ui.kortz.request: Buyer’s Request (3 items the buyer asks for)
ui.kortz.entry.skylight: rappel from the roof • stealth route
ui.kortz.prep.guard: see the guards on the map
ui.kortz.get.caracara: armored pickup in the car park
ui.kortz.get.noneD: hit the road and find your own car
ui.kortz.eliteHint: Under 17:00 • accuracy >90% • little damage to the loot • Buyer’s Request complete
ui.kortz.note: Kortz has no percentage cuts – the host keeps the whole haul. Crew members get a fixed payment from the game of roughly $100k–200k each (player reports), so take turns hosting.
ui.kortz.tip.first: The first main painting sold after the Thursday reset is the biggest chunk of this heist. Keep that run clean – don't risk failing it for extra secondary loot.
ui.kortz.tip.notFirst: The week's second painting sells for about a quarter of the first. If you've used it up, another heist that still has its weekly bonus pays better.
ui.kortz.tip.loading: Loading Bay is the farming route: drive the Alpha Mail van in and you start right by the server room, no walking down several floors.
ui.kortz.tip.sewer: The Sewer route needs a new sewer key every run (5 random spots outside) – searching in the open for long risks guards spotting you before you're even inside.
ui.kortz.tip.skylight: Skylight suits pure-stealth Elite runs. Night vision helps a lot, but you have to work your way down from the top floor.
ui.kortz.tip.staff: Staff Entrance is good for a first run to learn the layout; switch to Loading Bay afterwards and you'll be much faster.
ui.kortz.tip.annihilator: Careful! There are reports of the NPC pilot crashing the Annihilator at pickup – the Manchez, the Caracara or grabbing a car on the road is safer.
ui.kortz.tip.solo: Solo players can't enter Exhibit Level 2 (it needs 2 people). If the Buyer’s Request is in that room, Elite is off the table this run – check during the Scope.
ui.kortz.tip.guard: Do Guard Routes – you'll see the guards on the minimap. Their patrols are fixed every run, so learn them once and you're set.
ui.kortz.tip.hard: Hard only opens on replays (pay $100k within about 15 minutes of Raf's call). The main painting only gains ~10%; the real prize is the $100k Elite.
ui.kortz.tip.witness: Living witnesses and camera footage lower the loot's value – always wipe the footage at the computer outside the vault before leaving, and allow at least 10 seconds in the vault.
ui.kortz.pro: Recommended setup applied: Loading Bay disguised as delivery staff, Guard Routes + EMP, escape on the Manchez, bags full of top-tier paintings, Buyer’s Request completed, and the run timed for the first sale of the week.
ui.cayo.tag: Infiltrate El Rubio's private island in the Kosatka submarine, steal the target from the compound vault, sweep secondary loot across the island and escape out to sea – a heist you can play solo from start to finish.
ui.cayo.primary: Primary target in El Rubio's vault
ui.cayo.primaryHint: Random from the Scope – the week's first run has a better chance of good loot.
ui.cayo.bagsHint: Average value per full bag; the type of secondary loot is random each run.
ui.cayo.veh.annihilator: stealth helicopter to the drop zones
ui.cayo.veh.patrol: armed boat to the main dock
ui.cayo.entryHint: Available points depend on the vehicle
ui.cayo.eliteHint: Finish within 15 minutes • everyone's bag full • no failed hacks
ui.cayo.noteFirst: The very first run (Madrazo Files) has no Fencing or Pavel deductions yet
ui.cayo.tip.madrazo: Your very first run always gives the Madrazo Files and skips the 12% deduction – fill your bags with secondary loot.
ui.cayo.tip.tequila: Got the Tequila? Don't be gutted – secondary loot gets a +20% boost this run. Fill your bags with cocaine and the money comes back.
ui.cayo.tip.panther: The Panther Statue only appears during events – when you see it, pay the setup fast enough to unlock Hard.
ui.cayo.tip.solo: Solo, you can't take the gold in the compound (it needs two people swiping keycards together) – cocaine is the best secondary loot alone.
ui.cayo.tip.gold: With {n} players gold is the best (~$446k per bag), but there's only so much gold on the island – top up with cocaine if it runs out.
ui.cayo.tip.drain: The classic route: Kosatka → swim into the drainage tunnel, cut the grate and come up inside the compound without fighting anyone.
ui.cayo.tip.tryDrain: If you're not confident yet, try Kosatka + Drainage Tunnel – the quietest and fastest route for stealth players.
ui.cayo.tip.airstrip: Escaping by the airstrip means passing lots of guards; one sighting and the whole island is on alert – swimming back to the Kosatka is easier.
ui.cayo.tip.day: In daytime guards see further – beginners should pick night.
ui.cayo.tip.silenced: Stealth runs want suppressed weapons: Conspirator or Saboteur, so nearby guards don't panic when you shoot.
ui.cayo.tip.aggressive: Aggressive works, but the shooting eats time so the 15-minute Elite slips easily, and it doesn't pay any more.
ui.cayo.tip.hard: For Hard you must pay the setup within 48 minutes of Pavel's call when the cooldown ends – miss it and it becomes Normal.
ui.cayo.tip.wantHard: For Hard, pay the setup within 48 minutes after the cooldown ends: the main target gets +10% and Elite becomes $100k.
ui.cayo.tip.weekly: Do one Cayo run after the Thursday reset – later Scopes in the same week mostly give Tequila.
ui.cayo.pro: Recommended setup applied: Kosatka → Drainage Tunnel at night, suppressed Conspirator, swim back to the submarine, Hard + Elite on, and everyone fills a bag with {loot}. Don't forget the safe in El Rubio's office.
ui.casino.tag: Lester's big job: crack the vault under the Diamond Casino & Resort. Go in quietly, in disguise or guns blazing, and hire NPC crew as gunman, driver and hacker.
ui.casino.firstHint: The multiplier comes from community testing; Rockstar never announced it
ui.casino.app.bigcon: walk in through the door in disguise
ui.casino.hackerHint: Works from outside and sets your vault time (if you're not detected). You still do every hack yourself.
ui.casino.gunmanHint: Doesn't come in with you – supplies the weapon loadouts. Barely affects the money.
ui.casino.driverHint: Doesn't drive for you – leaves the getaway vehicles at the switch point. Barely affects the money.
ui.casino.entryHint: Must be unlocked during the Scope first
ui.casino.hitsHint: Each hit while carrying loot loses about $2,000 from the bag
ui.casino.eliteSs: Under 15:00 • nobody dies • never detected • no failed hacks
ui.casino.note: Minimum cut is 15% each • this assumes a full take; if you run out of vault time the real total is lower
ui.casino.tip.first: The week's first run (after the Thursday reset) pays about 1.86× – more than all crew savings combined. Schedule the team for that day.
ui.casino.tip.rickie: Rickie is the cheapest, but he gives the shortest vault time – the money you can't grab costs more than you save on his fee.
ui.casino.tip.yohan: Yohan (5%) gives 2:52, but Christian Feltz (7%) gives 3:00 and doesn't need a Nightclub – Feltz is better value.
ui.casino.tip.cheapCrew: The gunman and driver barely affect the money – Karl + Karim (5% + 5%) add another {n}% to the pool.
ui.casino.tip.ss: Silent & Sneaky means never being seen – get detected on the way and you lose about a minute of vault time.
ui.casino.tip.bigcon: The Big Con is the best balance of speed and safety; the Gruppe Sechs outfit is the farmers' favourite.
ui.casino.tip.aggr: Aggressive has the fastest setup, but every hit while carrying loot is money lost, and Elite needs 80 headshots.
ui.casino.tip.diamonds: Diamonds only appear in event weeks – if the Scope shows them, don't miss it. Combined with the week's first run it's the ceiling for this heist.
ui.casino.tip.gold2: Gold with 2 players: gold is heavy and slow to grab, so pick a long-timer hacker (Paige/Avi) to carry nearly all of it.
ui.casino.tip.buyerLow: The Low Level buyer is the furthest away – a longer police chase. Pick High Level if you can.
ui.casino.pro: Recommended setup applied: The Big Con in Gruppe Sechs outfits through the main door, cheap Karl + Karim, Paige Harris with 3:25, the High Level buyer, and the run timed for the first of the week (use Avi if you have him).
ui.doom.tag: A three-act epic from an underground Facility: hunt down data, storm Bogdan's submarine and finish by stopping the AI about to launch missiles at the city.
ui.doom.ec.a1: Finish within 15:00 | Vehicle damage under 10% | Nobody dies
ui.doom.ec.a2: Finish within 15:00 | Vehicle damage under 5% | Nobody dies
ui.doom.tip.a3: Act III is the longest (a 45–60 minute finale) but pays the most of the three. Elite needs 150 headshots, so the team needs sharp shooters.
ui.doom.tip.a2: Act II Elite means finishing in 15 minutes with under 5% vehicle damage – put your best driver behind the wheel.
ui.doom.tip.a1: Act I is the shortest and easiest – a good warm-up for a new team before the bigger acts.
ui.doom.tip.firstHost: The first-run bonus is tied to the host – if teammates haven't done it this week, take turns hosting to collect the bonus several times.
ui.doom.tip.notFirst: If the host hasn't played this act this week it pays about 1.22× – let whoever hasn't done it host.
ui.doom.tip.hard: Hard pays 25% more than Normal and the enemies are tougher – bring full armour.
ui.doom.tip.wantHard: Teams that know the acts can switch to Hard for an instant +25%.
ui.doom.tip.setups: Doomsday setup missions got a pay raise in update 1.73, so doing every step yourself isn't wasted.
ui.doom.pro: Recommended setup applied: Act III on Hard as the week's first run – Doomsday's biggest payday. The team needs to be ready to play for about an hour.
ui.og.tag: GTA Online's first set of heists, run from a High-end Apartment: from robbing a Fleeca bank all the way to the big Pacific Standard job. You need a full team for every role.
ui.og.ec.fleeca: Finish within 5:20 | Vehicle damage under 6% | Nobody dies
ui.og.ec.prison: Rashkovsky takes no more than 1% damage | Get him out within 4:40 | Nobody dies
ui.og.ec.humane: Finish within 11:00 | Vehicle damage under 2% | Nobody dies
ui.og.ec.seriesa: Finish within 6:30 | Kill 75 enemies | Nobody dies
ui.og.ec.pacific: Finish within 10:15 | Don't let NOOSE get called | Nobody dies
ui.og.tip.pacific: Pacific Standard Elite: finish in 10:15 without NOOSE being called – the hacker can't miss, and the bike team mustn't get lost on the escape.
ui.og.tip.fleeca: Fleeca needs only 2 players and is quick – the best heist for newcomers to practise teamwork.
ui.og.tip.prison: Prison Break Elite: Rashkovsky can take no more than 1% damage, so his escort has to drive very smoothly.
ui.og.tip.humane: Humane Labs Elite: under 2% vehicle damage – the Insurgent driver has to watch every corner.
ui.og.tip.seriesa: Series A Elite needs 75 kills – everyone shoots, don't leave it all to one player.
ui.og.tip.firstHost: The ×1.5 bonus is counted per host – take turns hosting the same heist to get it several times a week.
ui.og.tip.notFirst: If the host hasn't done this finale this week, you instantly get 50% more.
ui.og.tip.wantHard: Regular teams can switch to Hard for 25% more than Normal; Easy pays only half.
ui.og.tip.hostCut: The host pays the setup and does the most setups, so it's customary to give the host a slightly bigger cut.
ui.og.pro: Recommended setup applied: Pacific Standard on Hard as the week's first run – the best-paying job of the Original set.
ui.g.title: Beginner guide
ui.g.intro: A heist is a big job split into parts: you prepare with short missions, then play the big final mission (the Finale) – that's where the money comes from. This guide explains the words you'll see in the game, and every heist on this page has a step-by-step section at the top.
ui.g.flow.buyD: Each heist starts from a property you own
ui.g.flow.scopeD: Look at the target and take photos
ui.g.flow.prepD: Short missions for vehicles, gear and info
ui.g.flow.payD: The haul is split by the cuts
ui.g.glossTitle: Words you'll see in the game
ui.g.tip1: Do preps in an invite-only session so other players can't ruin them.
ui.g.tip2: Go slow and stay unseen – getting detected or dying costs more time than being careful.
ui.g.tip3: Plan on this page, then make the same choices on the in-game board.
ui.g.tip4: Look for the icons shown in the steps on your map – they mark where each heist starts.
ui.g.tip5: Need a team? Invite friends or crew members from the board, or open the job to matchmaking. Cayo Perico can be done solo.
ui.g.howTitle: New to this heist? Step by step
ui.g.imgCredit: Pictures: vehicle renders and radar icons from the FiveM docs, overhead photos cropped from this site's map images.
ui.g.mapPhoto: Overhead view of the selected spot
ui.g.def.host: The player who starts the heist and pays the setup cost. The money goes through the host, who sets everyone's cut.
ui.g.def.scope: A recon mission: go to the target, look around and photograph things with the phone camera. Whatever you find – entrances, guards, loot – becomes a choice on the planning board. You don't steal anything in a Scope.
ui.g.def.setup: The start of a heist: paying the start fee and the missions that unlock the Finale. The 'setup cost' is the fee the host pays.
ui.g.def.prep: A short mission that gets something for the Finale: a vehicle, weapons, a keycard, a disguise. Required preps must be done; optional ones make the Finale easier.
ui.g.def.finale: The last and longest mission – the actual robbery. You only get paid when the Finale succeeds.
ui.g.def.approach: How you'll do the robbery: quietly (stealth), in disguise or guns blazing. It changes which preps you need.
ui.g.def.primary: The main loot in the vault – most of the money comes from it.
ui.g.def.secondary: Extra loot you carry in your bag (gold, cash, paintings…). Optional, but it adds up.
ui.g.def.cut: Each player's percentage of the haul. The host sets it on the board; the minimum is usually 15% per player.
ui.g.def.elite: Extra goals for the Finale (finish fast, nobody dies…). Complete them all for a bonus paid to every player.
ui.g.def.hard: Difficulty. Hard pays more and has tougher enemies; in some heists Hard is only offered if you start the next run soon after the last one.
ui.g.def.firstweek: Many heists pay a bonus for the host's first Finale after the weekly reset (Thursday).
ui.g.def.cooldown: The waiting time after a Finale before the host can start the same heist again.
ui.g.def.fencing: A cut taken by whoever sells the stolen goods for you (e.g. Madrazo in Cayo Perico).
ui.g.def.board: Where you choose and launch everything. It's inside the heist's property (submarine, arcade basement, facility, apartment…).
ui.g.def.detected: A guard or camera has seen you. In stealth plans the alarm goes off and the Finale gets harder, slower or pays less.
ui.g.def.getaway: The escape after the robbery – usually in vehicles you prepared in a prep.
ui.g.def.buyer: Where you deliver the loot at the end of the Finale.
ui.g.def.invite: A lobby with only you and the friends you invite – no strangers to attack you during preps. Pause menu → Online → Find New Session → Invite Only Session.
ui.g.def.blip: An icon on the radar and the pause-menu map. The icons in these steps are the ones to look for in the game.
ui.g.cayo.s1: Buy the Kosatka submarine from the Warstock Cache & Carry website (in-game internet). It is the base of this heist.
ui.g.cayo.s2: Request the Kosatka (Interaction menu → Services), get on board and use the planning screen inside. Pavel, the captain, guides you.
ui.g.cayo.s3: Scope (Gather Intel): go to the island and find the primary target (Pavel tells you where). While you're there, photograph extra spots: entry points, compound entrances, escape points, secondary loot and tools (bolt cutters, grappling equipment, guard clothing). Every photo unlocks that option. Then leave the island.
ui.g.cayo.s4: Preps: do the preps the screen marks as required for your plan (approach vehicle, weapons, equipment). The Kosatka needs no vehicle prep. Optional 'disruption' preps weaken the guards.
ui.g.cayo.s5: Finale: land at your entry point, grab secondary loot if you like, get into the compound, open the vault and take the primary target, empty the safe in El Rubio's office, then escape. Stay unseen.
ui.g.cayo.s6: After the Finale wait for the cooldown. Every new run starts again with the Scope.
ui.g.casino.s1: Requirements: own an Arcade (Maze Bank Foreclosures website) and be a CEO, VIP or MC President. Registering as a VIP (Interaction menu → SecuroServ) needs $50,000 in the bank.
ui.g.casino.s2: Go down to the Arcade's basement: the planning room has three boards – Setup, Prep and Finale – used in that order.
ui.g.casino.s3: Board 1 (Setup) – Scope: follow Lester's instructions into the Diamond Casino to find out what's in the vault, then photograph the access points (entrances) and points of interest around the casino with your phone camera. Then choose your approach and pay the setup fee.
ui.g.casino.s4: Board 2 (Prep): hire the gunman, driver and hacker (they take a percentage – see below) and do the preps required for your approach. Optional preps such as patrol routes make the Finale easier.
ui.g.casino.s5: Board 3 (Finale): choose the entrance, exit and buyer, then start. Two players swipe keycards together to open the vault area, grab as much as you can before the vault timer ends, get out, switch to the getaway vehicles and deliver to the buyer.
ui.g.doom.s1: Requirements: own a Facility (Maze Bank Foreclosures website). The heist is planned on the screen inside it.
ui.g.doom.s2: There are three acts. Each act has its own prep and setup missions, then a Finale. The first time, play them in order: Act I → Act II → Act III.
ui.g.doom.s3: The Finales need 2–4 real players. The host pays each act's setup fee and sets the cuts before the Finale.
ui.g.og.s1: Requirements: a High-end Apartment and rank 12 or higher. Lester calls you to begin.
ui.g.og.s2: Use the planning board in the apartment. Each heist has several setup missions and then the Finale; start with The Fleeca Job, then the others unlock in order.
ui.g.og.s3: Every mission needs real players – Fleeca 2, the others 4 – and each player gets a role such as hacker, driver or gunman.
ui.g.kortz.s1: Requirements: a Mansion with the Art Studio – the forged painting you swap in is made there.
ui.g.kortz.s2: Scope: check the vault and where the Buyer’s Request items are. Solo players can't open Exhibit Level 2 (it needs two people).
ui.g.kortz.s3: Preps: choose an entrance – each needs its own prep (e.g. the Loading Bay uses an Alpha Mail disguise, the Sewer a hazmat suit and a sewer key) – plus optional preps such as Guard Routes or EMP Charges.
ui.g.kortz.s4: Finale: reach the basement vault, swap the real painting for your forgery, take extra art, wipe the camera footage at the computer outside the vault, then escape and deliver to Alec in Cypress Flats.
ui.g.kortz.note: Kortz Center is new (Title Update 1.73); these steps only use what's known on this page – check the in-game board for anything else.
ui.g.scopeHint: Every spot below comes from the game's own planning screen. Tools and secondary loot appear in only some of these places each run – the list shows every possible spot. Tap one to see it on the map.
ui.g.scopeHintKortz: Every spot below comes from the game's own Scope mission. The game's texts aren't in the script, so the names are worked out: Staff Entrance and Skylight (the four roof spots) are clear, Loading Bay and Sewer come from where they are. Tap one to see it on the map.
ui.g.scopeAll: Show every Scope spot on the map
ui.g.chIntro: The Original Heists and the Doomsday Heist have one-time challenges for playing the whole set in a certain way. They pay on top of the normal heist money – the hardest and best known is Criminal Mastermind, often shortened to CMM.
ui.g.def.allinorder: Finish every Finale of the set in its original order (Original: The Fleeca Job → The Pacific Standard Job; Doomsday: Act I → Act III).
ui.g.def.loyalty: Play the whole set with the same team of players.
ui.g.def.cmm: All in Order + Loyalty, on Hard, and nobody on the team dies at any point – setup missions included. The toughest challenge in GTA Online, with a one-time bonus worth millions for each player.
ui.g.chTip1: Agree on the team before you start – swapping a player breaks Loyalty and Criminal Mastermind.
ui.g.chTip2: One death anywhere fails Criminal Mastermind and you have to start again from the first heist. Play slowly, use cover and keep your armour full.
ui.g.chTip3: You can earn All in Order, Loyalty and Criminal Mastermind in the same run – and Elite Challenges along the way.
ui.g.chTip4: Each challenge pays only once per character.
ui.g.og.s4: Challenges: finishing all five heists in order (All in Order), with the same team (Loyalty) – and all of that on Hard without anyone dying (Criminal Mastermind) – pays big one-time bonuses. See the beginner guide.
ui.g.doom.s4: Challenges: playing all three acts in order (All in Order), with the same team (Loyalty) – and all of that on Hard without anyone dying (Criminal Mastermind) – pays big one-time bonuses. See the beginner guide.
ui.g.def.take: The total value of the loot before anyone's cut. The board shows the 'potential take' before the Finale.
ui.g.def.lobby: The host launches the mission from the board; the others join the lobby, pick their outfit and press Ready.
ui.g.def.role: A job inside the team, such as hacker, driver, gunman or pilot. In the Original Heists each real player gets one.
ui.g.def.vault: The locked room where the primary target is kept.
ui.g.def.keycard: A card that opens locked doors. Some doors need two players to swipe at the same time.
ui.g.def.hacking: Short minigames you play yourself to open doors, keypads and computers (e.g. matching fingerprints).
ui.g.def.thermal: An explosive you stick on a locked door to burn it open.
ui.g.def.drill: Used to open safety-deposit boxes or a vault door – keep it steady and don't overheat it.
ui.g.def.disguise: An outfit that lets you walk past guards without being attacked.
ui.g.def.loadout: The set of weapons you bring into the Finale.
ui.g.def.wanted: Police stars. Lose them by leaving the search area before you deliver the loot.
ui.g.def.lives: Shared lives in a Finale. Each death uses one; when they run out, the mission fails.
ui.g.def.retry: After a failed mission the team can usually retry from the last checkpoint instead of starting over.

ui.g.cas.hint: There are no map spots for the Casino: the game's scripts don't say which position is which access point, so here is a checklist instead. Everything is photographed with the phone camera, from outside the casino and from its roof.
ui.g.cas.req: the scope mission on the Setup board. Follow Lester's instructions inside the casino; it shows what's in the vault (cash, artwork, gold or diamonds).
ui.g.cas.acc: every one you photograph can be picked as an entrance or exit on the Finale board.
ui.g.cas.byApproach: Which approach can use which entrance (the same as the board above):
ui.g.cas.poi: extra photos around the casino for Lester's board. They're optional – you don't need them to start the heist.
ui.g.cas.tip1: Photograph as many access points as you can in one trip – more entrances and exits to choose from on the Finale board.
ui.g.cas.tip2: The roof access points are hard to reach on foot – fly over the casino and take the photos from the air.
ui.g.cas.tip3: Do the scope in an invite-only session so nobody attacks you while you hold the camera.
ui.g.cas.prepTitle: Optional preps that make the Finale easier
ui.g.cas.prepHint: Which ones you can do depends on the approach – the Prep board shows them.
ui.g.cas.prep.patrol: shows where the guards walk inside.
ui.g.cas.prep.duggan: destroy the shipments to weaken the casino guards.
ui.g.cas.prep.pass: a security keycard that opens more doors without hacking.
ui.g.cas.prep.emp: (Silent & Sneaky) cuts the power for a while so cameras and lasers go off.
ui.g.cas.prep.suits: (Silent & Sneaky) outfits that make you harder to spot.
ui.tr.title: Pro tricks
ui.tr.note: Community tips and player experience, not official data. The game is patched often, so check the in-game board before you rely on a detail.
ui.tr.addPrompt: Write the trick (one or two short sentences):
ui.tr.added: Trick added. Everyone sees it after GitHub Pages rebuilds (about 1 minute).
ui.tr.cas.t.cash: Cash pays the least and takes the most grabbing – skip it if the vault offers anything else.
ui.tr.cas.t.art: Artwork is the usual pick for 2 players: it pays only a little less than gold and is quicker to take.
ui.tr.cas.t.gold2: Gold pays the most of the three but fills a bag slowly. With 2 players it only works with a long-vault-time hacker (Paige or Avi) – otherwise take artwork.
ui.tr.cas.t.gold3: Gold is the best target with 3–4 players: more hands fill the bags before the vault timer runs out.
ui.tr.cas.t.dia: Diamonds only appear in event weeks and pay the most – if the Scope shows them, take them and ignore the rest.
ui.tr.cas.t.vault: Vault order: fill your bags with the main target first. Only if time is left, drill the deposit boxes (needs the Power Drills prep, $0–10,000 per box). Head for the door when about 15 seconds remain.
ui.tr.cas.t.duo: 2 players: one of you takes the hacks and doors while the other starts grabbing right away – don't wait for each other.
ui.tr.cas.t.ss: Silent & Sneaky: failing hacks too many times counts as being detected, so give the hacking to your steadiest player.
ui.tr.cas.t.staff: Staff Lobby is the quiet way in (and out): few guards patrol it. A stun gun switches off the camera by the side door.
ui.tr.cas.t.tunnel: Security Tunnel is a favourite for the Big Con: a service route that avoids the casino floor.
ui.tr.cas.t.main: The Main Door crosses the busiest floor. It really only suits a disguised Big Con – to stay unseen, pick the Staff Lobby.
ui.tr.cas.t.fire: Firefighter exit: do the Firefighter Gear prep first – steal a fire truck from one of the fire stations highlighted on your map (it gives a 3-star wanted level; other stations don't count). After the vault, change into the outfits and walk out as rescue staff; follow the game's marker to the changing spot (one guide says the laundry room).
ui.tr.cas.t.noose: NOOSE exit: the prep means going into the police station's restricted area – one guide reports a 4-star wanted level for that, so it is riskier than the firefighter outfit. One guide recommends it for the Big Con.
ui.tr.cas.p1: Stun gun = camera off. Carry one in your loadout: it switches a camera off for a moment, which is how one walkthrough gets past the camera at the Staff Lobby door.
ui.tr.cas.p2: Scope every access point you can in one trip. You can only choose entrances and exits you photographed, so a full set means a free choice on the Finale board.
ui.tr.cas.p3: Exit disguises compared: Firefighter = steal a fire truck from a highlighted fire station (3 stars). NOOSE = enter the police station's restricted area (about 4 stars, riskier). Do the prep before the Finale.
ui.tr.kor.t.staff: Staff Entrance is the easiest first run: simple Scope and gear prep, but you start on the upper floor and work down. A stun gun switches off cameras.
ui.tr.kor.t.loading: Loading Bay with the Alpha Mail disguise is the best all-round (and solo) route: drive in as delivery staff, nobody stops you, and you start closest to the vault.
ui.tr.kor.t.sewer: Sewer is the quietest: you surface in the basement with few guards or cameras. The catch: the manhole key spawns at random on a construction table outside, and one guide warns your health drains while you move through the sewer – bring full armour.
ui.tr.kor.t.sky: Skylight means coming down from the roof, so you work from the top floor to the vault – a good fit for stealth runs, and night vision helps.
ui.tr.kor.t.quiet: For a no-alarm run, one guide pairs the Sewer or the Skylight with the Military loadout – a good base for the Elite challenge.
ui.tr.kor.p1: Stun gun = camera off. Some Kortz guides rely on it at the Staff Entrance and on stealth routes.
ui.tr.kor.p2: Scope all four entrances in one go (Staff Entrance, Loading Bay, Sewer, Skylight) so you can change route later without another Scope.
ui.tr.cay.t.drain: Drainage Tunnel: swim in behind the compound, cut the grate with the cutting torch and come up inside – the quietest route and the easiest for a solo run. Photograph the tunnel in Scope or it won't be offered.
ui.tr.cay.t.dock: Main Dock is the usual exit for solo runs: carry the loot to the water and leave by boat.
ui.tr.cay.t.solo: Solo, you can't open the compound's gold room (it needs two people swiping keycards together), so fill your bag with the loot you can reach.
ui.tr.cay.t.gold: With 2+ players, gold is the most valuable secondary loot – take it, using two keycards to open the compound room.
ui.tr.cay.t.night: A night start makes guards notice you later – the common choice for stealth and for first solo runs.
ui.tr.cay.p1: A solo run wants both the drainage tunnel and the main dock in your Scope photos – if they are missing from the board, you didn't photograph them.
ui.pc.casino.loc.main.p: Straight through – nothing to learn, and a Big Con disguise lets you stroll through.
ui.pc.casino.loc.main.c: The busiest floor: the most guards and cameras, so one slip is seen by many people.
ui.pc.casino.loc.staff.p: Few guards patrol it – the usual pick for Silent & Sneaky, and a quiet way out for most approaches.
ui.pc.casino.loc.staff.c: Needs the side door scoped, and a stun gun is the common way to switch off the camera there.
ui.pc.casino.loc.tunnel.p: A service route away from the casino floor – a favourite for the Big Con.
ui.pc.casino.loc.waste.p: A back-of-house service route away from the casino floor.
ui.pc.casino.loc.waste.c: Not available for the Big Con.
ui.pc.casino.loc.sewer.p: Underground and away from the casino floor – guides mention it as an escape route too.
ui.pc.casino.loc.sewer.c: Not available for the Big Con, and it must be scoped first.
ui.pc.casino.loc.roof.p: Away from the casino floor and its guards.
ui.pc.casino.loc.roof.c: The roof access points are hard to reach on foot – scope them from a helicopter.
ui.pc.casino.exitd.fire.p: Walk out as rescue staff once you've left the vault.
ui.pc.casino.exitd.fire.c: Needs the Firefighter Gear prep: steal a fire truck from a highlighted fire station (3-star wanted level).
ui.pc.casino.exitd.noose.p: Blend in as police on the way out.
ui.pc.casino.exitd.noose.c: Needs the NOOSE Gear prep: a trip into the police station's restricted area (one guide reports 4 stars) – riskier than the firefighter outfit.
ui.pc.casino.app.ss.p: No alarm if you're never spotted – the cleanest run, with no police to deal with.
ui.pc.casino.app.ss.c: One detection ruins it, and failing hacks too many times counts as being detected.
ui.pc.casino.app.bigcon.p: The most forgiving: walk in disguised instead of sneaking.
ui.pc.casino.app.bigcon.c: Do something suspicious and your cover is blown.
ui.pc.casino.app.aggr.p: Quick to set up, and you can use heavy weapons.
ui.pc.casino.app.aggr.c: Police and guards fight you, every hit while carrying loot costs money, and Elite needs 80 headshots.
ui.pc.cayo.entry.drain.p: The quietest route – cut the grate and come up inside the compound; the easiest solo entry.
ui.pc.cayo.entry.drain.c: Kosatka only, and the tunnel must be found in Scope.
ui.pc.cayo.entry.airstrip.c: Plenty of guards – one sighting alerts the whole island.
ui.pc.cayo.escape.kosatka.p: Swim out to the submarine – easy and quiet.
ui.pc.cayo.escape.airstrip.c: Lots of guards on the way – one sighting alerts everyone; swimming back to the Kosatka is easier.
ui.pc.cayo.escape.maindock.p: The usual solo exit: leave by boat from the main dock.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.staff.p: Easiest for a first run: simple Scope and gear prep.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.staff.c: You start on the upper floor and work down.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.loading.p: Best all-round and solo: drive in as delivery staff (Alpha Mail) and start closest to the vault.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.sewer.p: Quietest: you surface in the basement with few guards or cameras.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.sewer.c: The manhole key spawns at random on a construction table outside, and one guide warns your health drains while you move through the sewer.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.skylight.p: A roof route for stealth and no-alarm runs, a good fit for Elite.
ui.pc.kortz.entry.skylight.c: You work down from the top floor, and night vision helps.
